feat: automate benchmark on PR requests using Github Actions (#1037)

This PR adds Github actions to automate benchmark running on PR requests

It will create a [Github Job
Summary](https://github.blog/news-insights/product-news/supercharging-github-actions-with-job-summaries/)
of the benchmark and add it to the benchmark action (see
https://github.com/moscajs/aedes/actions/runs/16239498783#summary-45853979456
)

The benchmark steps run serialized in the hope that performance on a
single runner does not vary too much.
I have been building testing this using
https://github.com/seriousme/aedes/pull/1 which also shows how it
operates.

It also shows that variation between results is inevitable, even when
running on the same runner and the Aedes code is identical !!

In https://github.com/seriousme/aedes/pull/1 I was able to add the
comment automatically to the PR using
`.github/actions/sticky-pr-comment/action.yml` however if you send a PR
from a fork the GITHUB_TOKEN that runs the actions by default (event:
[pull_request](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/events-that-trigger-workflows#pull_request)
) only has `read` access on the PR for security reasons (see [Pull
Request events for forked
repositories](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/events-that-trigger-workflows#pull-request-events-for-forked-repositories))

This can be fixed by attaching to the event:
[pull_request_target](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/events-that-trigger-workflows#pull_request_target),
however Github notes explicitly: *Avoid using this event if you need to
build or run code from the pull request.*

So for now I used Github Job Summary instead.

Kind regards,
Hans

This PR migrates Aedes to ESM.
I followed Sindre Sorhus' checklist mentioned by Daniel in #1038:

- [X] Add "type": "module" to your package.json 
- [X] Replace "main": "index.js" with "exports": "./index.js" in your
package.json.
- [X] Update the "engines" field in package.json to Node.js 20: "node":
">=20".
- [X] Remove 'use strict'; from all JavaScript files.
- [X] Replace all require()/module.export with import/export.
- [X] Use only full relative file paths for imports: import x from '.';
→ import x from './index.js';.
- [X] If you have a TypeScript type definition (for example,
index.d.ts), update it to use ESM imports/exports.
- [X] Use the [node:
protocol](https://nodejs.org/api/esm.html#esm_node_imports) for Node.js
built-in imports.

And added the following items:
- [X] remove `proxyquire` as it does not work with ESM (Proxy-require,
the name says it all)
- [X] monkey patch neostandard in eslint.config.js as it does not
support import assertions yet (I opened a ticket with them, but this
works)
- [X] add `test/require.cjs` which checks if `require("aedes")` still
works for those that need it.

Enjoy!
Hans

of the heavy lifting.

feat: add `drainTimeout` option to protect against slow/frozen clients (#1060)

When a client's TCP buffer fills and it stops reading, the broker waits
indefinitely for the 'drain' event, blocking message delivery to ALL
subscribers.

This proof of concept implements a drainTimeout option (disabled by
default for backwards compatibility) that sets a maximum time to wait
for drain. After the timeout, the slow client is disconnected and
delivery continues.

Changes:
- Add drainTimeout option to Aedes constructor (default: 0 = disabled)
   - Implement drain timeout logic in lib/write.js
   - Add TypeScript type definition
   - Add comprehensive tests (unit + E2E with readStop() + ToxiProxy)
   - Update documentation with recommendations
   
The solution based on timeouts might not be ideal but brings a quick fix
on the table for this issue and is good enough to start the discussion.

fix: add .js extensions to .d.ts imports for node16 resolution (#1083)

## Summary
- Adds `.js` extensions to all relative imports in `.d.ts` type
definition files
- Fixes TypeScript `moduleResolution: "node16"` failing to resolve types
when importing `aedes`

Closes #1082

## Details

With `moduleResolution: "node16"` and `"type": "module"`, TypeScript
strictly requires file extensions on relative imports. PR #1081 added
the `types` condition to `package.json` exports, allowing TypeScript to
find the entry `aedes.d.ts`, but the internal relative imports within
the `.d.ts` files still lacked `.js` extensions, causing resolution
failures.

**Files changed:**
- `aedes.d.ts` — entry point re-exports
- `types/client.d.ts` — imports from `packet` and `instance`
- `types/instance.d.ts` — imports from `client` and `packet`
- `types/packet.d.ts` — imports from `client`
- `test/types/aedes.test-d.ts` — test import from `types/packet`

chore: reduce production dependencies (#1045)

@robertsLando 
As promised, this PR reduces the number of production dependencies to a
bare minimum.

This PR replaces:
1. "end-of-stream" by native "finished" from "node:stream" 
2. "fastfall" by a local  "runfall" 
3. "fastparallel":  by a local "runParallel" 
4. "fastseries": by a local "runSeries" 
5. "hyperid": by "randomUUID" from 'node:crypto' , hyperid might be
faster (25M ops/second vs 12M ops/second) but also creates predictable
ID's and since we only used "hyperid" to generate clientID's 12M
ops/second should still be enough imo)
6. "retimer": by a local "retimer" which is nearly as fast as the
original "retimer" module with a difference of 1 second on 1M
invocations.
7. "reusify": by a local "ObjectPool" (btw: reusify was only used on
"Enquers" and I am not sure how much performance this actually added as
V8 has optimized object creation over time, but just to be sure I put in
the ObjectPool)
8. "uuid": by "randomUUID" from 'node:crypto' as it turned out that on
nodeJS the "uuidv4" of "uuid" it is an alias for "randomUUID" from
'node:crypto' anyway.

The local variants listed above are all quite small, mostly because they
only need to support one variant instead of the many variants that some
external modules provide. Also over the years some patterns have become
more easy to implement with modern Javascript.

This PR tries to keep the code changes to a minimum.
From here on, further optimizations might be possible, but I didn't want
to make this PR too complex.

Kind regards,
Hans

types: add missing decodeProtocol, trustProxy, trustedProxies to AedesOptions (#1093)

Closes #1089.

Three constructor options are read in the `aedes.js` constructor and
have `defaultOptions` entries, but were missing from the `AedesOptions`
interface in `types/instance.d.ts`, so a TypeScript caller passing any
of them got a type error:

- `decodeProtocol` (default `null`)
- `trustProxy` (default `false`)
- `trustedProxies` (default `[]`)

### Change
- Add the three to `AedesOptions`. `trustProxy: boolean`,
`trustedProxies: string[]`, and a `DecodeProtocolHandler` for
`decodeProtocol` — typed permissively (`(client, buffer) => any`) since
it's consumed by external transports (e.g. aedes-server-factory) and has
no fixed return contract here. Happy to tighten it if you have a
canonical signature in mind.
- Exercise all three in `test/types/aedes.test-d.ts` to prevent
re-drift.

Types-only / no runtime change. Pre-existing (not MQTT 5.0-related);
split out of #1088 to keep that PR's scope tight, as agreed. `tsd`
green.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

Merge commit from fork

* fix: reject topics with too many levels to prevent DoS crash

A remote client could crash the broker (uncaught exception) by sending a
PUBLISH/SUBSCRIBE/UNSUBSCRIBE, or setting a Will, with a deeply nested topic.
qlobber (used via mqemitter and the persistence trie) throws a synchronous
'too many words' error once a topic exceeds its max_words limit (default 100),
and aedes did not guard the mq.on / mq.emit / mq.removeListener calls, so the
throw propagated to the event loop and terminated the process.

Add a configurable maxTopicLevels option (default 100, matching qlobber's
limit) and reject over-limit topics at broker.publish/subscribe/unsubscribe
before they reach qlobber, returning a graceful error instead of crashing.

Fixes GHSA-xxqp-5qx8-gj5q

* fix: harden maxTopicLevels guard after self-review

- clamp maxTopicLevels to [1, 100]; 100 is a hard ceiling because the
  bundled mqemitter/aedes-persistence pin qlobber at max_words=100, so a
  higher value would pass the guard yet still crash in the matcher
- validate topic depth at the protocol boundary too (validateTopic for
  SUBSCRIBE/UNSUBSCRIBE, handlePublish for PUBLISH) so over-limit topics
  are rejected before any persistence side-effect or PUBACK/PUBREC, with
  a consistent 'topic has too many levels' error; the broker.publish/
  subscribe/unsubscribe guard remains for the will and direct-API paths
- guard topicLevelCount against non-string topics (no TypeError)
- note the '/'-separator assumption
- tests: level boundary (100 ok / 101 rejected), clamp of >100 and 0,
  persistent-session SUBSCRIBE, QoS 1/2 PUBLISH (no ack before reject)
- docs/types updated for the clamped range

feat: MQTT 5.0 support (#1088)

## What

Adds MQTT 5.0 support to the broker. MQTT 3.1/3.1.1 behaviour is
unchanged throughout. Implemented incrementally; each feature is
exercised end-to-end against a real `mqtt@5` client over TCP in
`test/mqtt5.js`.

Top-level: closes #194. Tracking issue: #821.

### Tracking issue #821 — per-feature status

A full spec-conformance review (against the [OASIS MQTT 5.0
spec](https://docs.oasis-open.org/mqtt/mqtt/v5.0/mqtt-v5.0.html)) is
recorded on #821. Summary of what this PR resolves vs. what is still
open:

**Closes (implemented & conformant):**
- Closes #825 — Server-initiated DISCONNECT (0x8E takeover / 0x8B
shutdown / 0x95 packet-too-large / 0x94 topic-alias / 0x82
protocol-error), v5-only; inbound DISCONNECT 0x04 will-handling correct
- Closes #826 — Payload Format Indicator + Content Type (forwarded)
- Closes #830 — User Properties (forwarded)
- Closes #831 — Maximum Packet Size (advertised + inbound reject;
broker→client size-split is advisory)
- Closes #836 — Server Keep Alive
- Closes #837 — Assigned Client Identifier
- Closes #835 — Will Delay Interval (capped by session expiry; reconnect
cancels)
- Closes #827 — Request/Response (Response Topic + Correlation Data
forwarded) — *minor: Response Topic wildcard not validated
([MQTT-3.3.2-14])*
- Closes #832 — Optional Server feature availability (Max QoS / Retain /
Wildcard / Subscription-ID advertised correctly) — *the
Shared-Subscription-Available flag interaction is tracked under #841*
- Closes #824 — Message Expiry Interval (queued + retained
recompute/drop; will-message expiry) — *minor: live delivery path does
not decrement the interval (waiting time ≈ 0)*
- Closes #840 — Topic Alias **inbound**
(resolve/register/strip-before-forward, alias-0 and over-max rejected) —
*outbound broker-assigned aliases not implemented (optional / MAY)*

**Partially addresses — left open in #821:**
- #822 Reason code on all ACKs —
CONNACK/SUBACK/UNSUBACK/server-DISCONNECT carry codes; **PUBREL/PUBCOMP
carry none**, PUBACK/PUBREC only emit 0x87, SUBACK uses coarse 0x80 (not
0x87/0x8F)
- #823 Reason String on ACKs — not implemented
- #828 Subscription Identifier — single-match works; **multiple matching
SIs collapse to one** ([MQTT-3.3.4-4]) and **retained-on-subscribe
deliveries don't echo the SI**
- #829 Flow control — Receive Maximum advertised + `0` rejected, but
**outbound in-flight is not capped** to the client's Receive Maximum
(§4.9)
- #833 Enhanced authentication — not implemented; **CONNECT
Authentication Method is silently ignored** (password auth succeeds
instead of 0x8C, §4.12)
- #834 Subscription Options — Max QoS / No Local / Retain As Published
implemented; **Retain Handling (1/2) ignored** ([MQTT-3.8.3-2])
- #838 Server Reference — not implemented
- #839 Session Expiry — full behaviour within a running broker (incl.
CONNACK echo of the clamped value); **not persisted across broker
restart** (the storage item this issue was opened for)
- #841 Shared Subscriptions — implemented **single-instance** on the
separate `sharedsubs` branch (persistence-backed, **not cluster-safe**);
**deferred in this PR** (advertised unavailable) pending the
cluster-aware rework. Until then a `$share/...` SUBSCRIBE should be
refused with 0x9E rather than accepted as a literal topic (§3.2.2.3.13 /
§4.8)

### Implemented

- **Handshake & framing** — accept `protocolVersion: 5`;
protocol-version-aware write path so v5 reason codes and properties are
serialized; CONNACK uses a reason code (mapped from the legacy return
codes)
- **Property pass-through** — v5 PUBLISH properties (user properties,
content type, response topic, correlation data, payload format)
forwarded to subscribers
- **Topic Alias** (inbound) + CONNACK `topicAliasMaximum` advertisement
- **Subscription Identifiers** — echoed on matching PUBLISHes; persisted
for non-clean sessions
- **Session Expiry Interval** — `cleanStart` vs persistence decoupled;
broker timers keep / wipe / expire sessions; reconnect cancels expiry;
clamped value echoed in CONNACK
- **Server-initiated DISCONNECT** — reason code `0x8E` on session
takeover, `0x8B` on broker shutdown
- **Will Delay Interval** — will published after the delay (capped by
session expiry); cancelled if the client reconnects
- **DISCONNECT with Will** (reason `0x04`)
- **UNSUBACK reason codes** (`0x00` / `0x11`)
- **Message Expiry Interval** — expired queued/retained messages
dropped; remaining lifetime recomputed on (queued/retained) delivery
- **Subscription options** — Maximum QoS, No Local, Retain As Published
- **Maximum Packet Size** — broker option advertised in CONNACK;
oversized inbound packets rejected with DISCONNECT `0x95`
- **Receive Maximum** — advertised in CONNACK (`0` rejected with `0x82`)
- **Not-authorized acks** — unauthorized v5 QoS > 0 publishes answered
with `0x87` PUBACK/PUBREC instead of dropping the connection; QoS 0
dropped silently with the connection kept up
- **Assigned Client Identifier** — returned in the CONNACK when the
broker generates an id for a client that connects with an empty client
id
- **Server Keep Alive** — a v5 client whose keepalive is unset or above
`keepaliveLimit` is not rejected; the broker imposes its limit via the
CONNACK `serverKeepAlive` property
- **DoS guards** — `maximumSessionExpiryInterval` (clamp) and
`maximumPendingSessions` (count cap) broker options
- **Types & docs** — new broker options added to the `AedesOptions` type
and documented in `docs/Aedes.md`

### Deliberately out of scope / not yet conformant (follow-ups — see
#821)

- **Shared subscriptions (#841)** — a **single-instance** implementation
exists on the separate `sharedsubs` branch (persistence-backed via
`addSharedSubscription`/`deliverShared`), but it is **deferred in this
PR**: the broker advertises `sharedSubscriptionAvailable: false`. A
cluster-correct version needs global group membership + deterministic
recipient selection coordinated via the persistence/emitter layer. (Open
item: a `$share` SUBSCRIBE should be refused with `0x9E` rather than
accepted as a literal topic.)
- **Receive Maximum enforcement (#829)** — outbound in-flight window;
advertised only, with existing `drainTimeout` providing transport
backpressure
- **Retain Handling 1/2 (#834)** — parsed but not yet honored on the
retained-delivery decision
- **Enhanced authentication / AUTH packet (#833)**
- **Reason String on ACKs (#823)**; broader/granular ACK reason codes
(#822) such as `0x10` no-matching-subscribers
- **Server reference (#838)**
- **Cross-restart durability of session-expiry & will-delay timers
(#839)** — needs persisted timestamps + a restart-time reaper, touching
the persistence backends
- **Outbound Topic Alias (#840)** — broker-assigned aliases on PUBLISHes
it sends

### Known conformance bugs to address before closing the umbrella issue
(#194)

- Inbound DISCONNECT **Session Expiry not validated** — a non-zero
Session Expiry on DISCONNECT is honored even when CONNECT declared `0`
(§3.14.2.2.2 / [MQTT-3.14.4-3]); the CONNECT value isn't retained for
the comparison
- `$share` accepted as a literal topic while advertised unavailable
([MQTT-3.2.2-23] / §4.8)
- Retain Handling 1/2 ignored ([MQTT-3.8.3-2])
- Multiple matching Subscription Identifiers collapsed to one
([MQTT-3.3.4-4])

## ⚠️ Dependencies — needs companion releases before merge

This depends on:
- moscajs/aedes-packet#192 — preserve `properties` + `messageExpiry`
- moscajs/aedes-persistence#108 — persist `subscriptionIdentifier` (+ a
conformance test confirming all backends already round-trip it, so no
backend code change is required)

`package.json` currently points `aedes-packet` / `aedes-persistence` at
the fork branches (with an `overrides` shim) so this branch installs and
runs standalone for review. **Before merge**, once the two companion
packages are released, this flips to published ranges and the shim is
removed. A `scripts/check-no-git-deps.js` release guard (wired into
release-it) blocks releasing while git deps remain.

## Tests

`test/mqtt5.js` (40 tests) drives a real `mqtt@5` client over TCP. Full
suite green (lint + tsd + unit), 0 failures / 0 cancelled.

ci: MQTT 5.0 + 3.1.1 compatibility workflow (Paho interop) (#1094)

## What

Adds a **MQTT compatibility** CI workflow that measures aedes's *actual*
MQTT 5.0
and 3.1.1 protocol compatibility by running the vendor-neutral
[Eclipse Paho interoperability
suite](https://github.com/eclipse-paho/paho.mqtt.testing)
(the same suite Mosquitto, EMQX and mochi-mqtt self-certify against) and
reports a
pass percentage as a sticky PR comment + job summary.

Unlike `test/mqtt5.js` (which drives aedes with the lenient `mqtt.js`
client against
our own reading of the spec), Paho uses a strict, independent client and
its own
packet de/serialiser — so it surfaces real interop gaps our own tests
miss.

Part of the MQTT 5.0 work (#821).

## How it works

```
aedes (this branch, tools/mqtt-compat/broker.js, :1883)
   ▲ TCP
run_compat.py ──> Paho client_test5.py (v5, 27 cases) + client_test.py (v3.1.1, 10)
   ├─ report.md  → sticky PR comment (<!-- MQTT_COMPAT_COMMENT -->) + job summary
   └─ result.json → uploaded artifact
```

- **`tools/mqtt-compat/broker.js`** — boots aedes on a TCP port with the
v5
capabilities the suite exercises enabled (inbound topic aliases) plus an
`authorizeSubscribe` rule that the `test_subscribe_failure` case
requires
  (matching the Paho reference broker's config).
- **`tools/mqtt-compat/run_compat.py`** — runs each Paho test in its
**own
subprocess with a hard timeout** (the Paho clients block with no
internal
timeout, so an unsupported feature would otherwise hang the whole run).
Pure
  stdlib. Emits a Markdown report + JSON.
- **`.github/workflows/mqtt-compat.yml`** — runs on `pull_request` and
`workflow_dispatch`; clones the suite at a pinned SHA, runs it, posts
the report.

## Results on this branch

| Protocol | Compatibility |
|----------|---------------|
| MQTT 5.0 | **62%** (16/26 evaluated) |
| MQTT 3.1.1 | **90%** (9/10) |

The percentage is **% of the Paho functional suite**, not "%
v5-compliant" — see
the coverage note below. Failures fall into three buckets:

**Expected gaps** (intentional / deferred-by-design per #821, annotated,
still
counted as fails):
- `shared_subscriptions` — advertised as unavailable
(`sharedSubscriptionAvailable=false`; #841).
- `flow_control1` — `receiveMaximum` advertised but not enforced
outbound (#829).
- `server_topic_alias` — broker-assigned (outbound) topic aliases not
implemented;
  inbound aliases work (#840, spec-optional/MAY).
- `subscribe_identifiers` — a delivery matching multiple overlapping
subscriptions
  echoes only one Subscription Identifier (#828, [MQTT-3.3.4-4]).

fix(connect): reject zero-length ClientId with CleanSession=0 on MQTT 3.1/3.1.1 (#1097)

## Summary

For MQTT 3.1.1 (and 3.1.0), a CONNECT with a **zero-length Client
Identifier** and **`CleanSession = 0`** must be rejected with CONNACK
return code `0x02` (Identifier rejected) and the connection closed.
aedes instead **accepted** it and assigned a generated id, regardless of
the clean flag.

Surfaced by the new MQTT compatibility workflow (Eclipse Paho interop
suite) — `test_zero_length_clientid` failed for v3.1.1.

Closes #1095

## Spec

> **[MQTT-3.1.3-7]** If the Client supplies a zero-byte ClientId, the
Client MUST also set CleanSession to 1.
>
> **[MQTT-3.1.3-8]** If the Client supplies a zero-byte ClientId with
CleanSession set to 0, the Server MUST respond to the CONNECT Packet
with a CONNACK return code 0x02 (Identifier rejected) and then close the
Network Connection.

(MQTT 3.1.1, §3.1.3.1 Client Identifier.)

## Fix

`init()` in `lib/handlers/connect.js` now sets `returnCode = 2`
alongside the other pre-acceptance checks when `protocolVersion < 5 &&
clientId.length === 0 && packet.clean === false`. The existing reject
path then sends the CONNACK and closes the connection.

The guard is gated on `protocolVersion < 5`, so **MQTT 5.0 is
intentionally unchanged**: a zero-length Client Identifier is still
allowed and the broker assigns one, reported via the Assigned Client
Identifier property (`client._assignedClientId`).

Behaviour matrix:

| version | clientId | clean | result |
|---|---|---|---|
| v3/v4 | empty | `false` | **rejected, return code 2** (new) |
| v3/v4 | empty | `true` | generated id (unchanged) |
| v3/v4 | non-empty | `false` | accepted (unchanged) |
| v5 | empty | any | assigned id via property (unchanged) |

## Tests

- `test/connect.js`: un-skipped and rewrote the previously-skipped
v3.1.1 reject test to assert the CONNACK return code is `2` and the
connection is closed (`connectionError` with `identifier rejected`,
`connectedClients === 0`).
- `test/connect.js`: added a v5 carve-out test confirming an empty
ClientId with `clean=false` still gets an assigned id (no rejection).
Both use raw bytes because mqtt-packet refuses to *encode* an empty
ClientId with `clean=false`.

Full unit suite passes (365 pass, 0 fail) and lint is clean.

ci: land MQTT compat comment handler on default branch (#1120)

Companion to #1118 (which targets `mqttv5`). Splits out the two pieces
that **must** live on the default branch for the fork-safe MQTT compat
comment to work.

## Why these belong on `main`

The **MQTT Compatibility** workflow (in #1118, on `mqttv5`) runs
untrusted fork code with a read-only token, so it can't post a PR
comment (fork PRs get a read-only `GITHUB_TOKEN`). The fork-safe pattern
is a `workflow_run` handler that runs from trusted base-repo code with
write scope. But GitHub only triggers a `workflow_run` handler **if its
file exists on the default branch**, and the handler resolves
`./.github/actions/*` from the default branch too. So two files have to
be on `main`:

- **`.github/workflows/mqtt-compat-comment.yml`** — the `workflow_run`
handler. Downloads the compat run's artifact and posts the sticky
comment. Never checks out or runs PR code; only `report.md` + the PR
number cross the trust boundary.
- **`.github/actions/sticky-pr-comment/action.yml`** — gains an optional
`pr-number` input (the `workflow_run` event payload has no
`pull_request` to read the number from) and paginates the comment lookup
so a busy PR doesn't get a duplicate. Backward compatible, and **nothing
on `main` consumes this action today**, so it disturbs nothing.

## What deliberately stays on `mqttv5` (#1118)

The compat **producer** (`mqtt-compat.yml`) — it runs from the PR's base
branch, and belongs with the 2.0 beta feature rather than booting the
broker + running the full Paho suite on every `main` PR.

## Activation

End-to-end commenting turns on once **both** this PR and #1118 are
merged: a `mqttv5` fork PR → `mqttv5`'s producer uploads the artifact →
this handler on `main` fires with a write token → checks out `main`
(updated action) → downloads the artifact → posts the comment.

client.subscriptions, client.duplicates, Aedes.clients, Aedes.brokers and the
SUBSCRIBE dedupe map were plain object literals keyed by strings that arrive
over the wire. A topic filter or Client ID named after an Object.prototype
property read back truthy, so every bare "is it already present?" check took
the "already present" branch on the very first packet and then called a method
on the inherited value.

Four confirmed remote crash variants, all unauthenticated under the default
hooks and all a single packet:

  SUBSCRIBE   "constructor"          -> addSubs takes the "subscription
                                        changed" branch, calls
                                        broker.unsubscribe(topic, undefined),
                                        mqemitter's assert(notify) throws
  UNSUBSCRIBE "constructor"          -> same throw from doUnsubscribe, and it
                                        needs no prior subscription at all
  CONNECT     clientId "__proto__"   -> registerClient calls .close() on
                                        Object.prototype
  $SYS .../new/clients with a        -> same registerClient lookup on every
  prototype-named payload               peer broker in a cluster

Plus two silent-corruption variants with no crash: _dedupe's
`map[sub.topic] = sub` reassigned the map's prototype for topic "__proto__"
instead of adding a key, so the subscription was dropped from the SUBSCRIBE;
and a peer broker id like "toString" read back truthy in Aedes.brokers, which
made aedes treat that broker as alive and aedes-persistence's willsByBrokers
suppress its wills forever.

Object.create(null) rather than Map: broker.clients and client.subscriptions
are read from userland with bracket access, so Map would be a breaking change
on a patch release. All in-repo access is bracket/delete/Object.keys/for...in;
there is no hasOwnProperty, instanceof Object, Object.assign or spread on
these stores. _dedupe's map is purely local with no API constraint, so it
becomes a real Map and loses its for...in.

Benchmarked on Node 22: the hot-path reads (deliverQoS, dedupe) cost ~1.7ns
more per op, and both stores take a `delete` in normal operation, which
dictionary-modes a plain {} anyway. No measurable steady-state regression.

BEHAVIOUR CHANGE for consumers reading these fields: broker.clients and
client.subscriptions no longer inherit from Object.prototype, so
`clients.hasOwnProperty(id)` throws and must become `Object.hasOwn(clients, id)`
or `id in clients`; `String(clients)` throws; `clients instanceof Object` is
false; util.inspect prints "[Object: null prototype]". Object.keys, for...in,
delete, JSON.stringify, spread and persistence.streamWill are unaffected.

fix: discard the QoS 2 dedup store on clean session (GHSA-p8r9-qf8w-p73r) (#1153)

Fixes GHSA-p8r9-qf8w-p73r.

**Needs `aedes-persistence` 11.0.0**, released 2026-09-16.

## The bug

MQTT 3.1.1 [MQTT-3.1.2-6] requires the server to discard all session
state when a client connects with
`cleanSession=1`. aedes cleared subscriptions but not the inbound QoS 2
dedup table, so a reused message
identifier from a previous session was acknowledged as a retransmission
per [MQTT-4.3.3-2] and never delivered
— `incomingGetPacket` still found the residue. A fresh clientId with the
same msgId is delivered normally, so
this is cross-session residue, not messageId exhaustion.

Trigger and full analysis are in the advisory; they stay there until it
publishes.

The outgoing queue was never affected — `emptyQueueFilter` already calls
`outgoingClearMessageId` when
`client.clean` is set. Incoming was the only part of the session that
survived.

## The fix

aedes cannot fix this alone: the persistence interface exposes incoming
packets only by `messageId`, and on a
clean reconnect aedes has no list of the previous session's ids (and in
a cluster, or after a restart, never had
one). So `aedes-persistence` gains `cleanIncoming(client)` and aedes
calls it.

Cleanup happens in **two** places, and both are needed:

1. **A new `cleanIncoming` connect action, running after
`registerClient`** — not alongside `cleanSubscriptions`
in `fetchSubs`. `registerClient` is where a previous client with the
same id is taken over [MQTT-3.1.4-2];
cleaning before it leaves a window in which the old client's in-flight
`incomingStorePacket` lands *after* the
wipe and restores the vulnerable state. This was caught in review with a
working repro.
2. **`Client#close`, for clean sessions** — a clean session ends with
the network connection, so waiting for a
reconnect that may never come leaves the entry behind forever. Measured
~91 KiB retained per vanished client;
repeated with fresh client ids it grows without bound, and on
mongodb/redis it survives restarts.

The persistence call is feature-detected so a persistence predating
`cleanIncoming` keeps working (and stays
vulnerable — stated plainly in `docs/MIGRATION.md`). It is wrapped in a
resolved promise because `runSeries` has
no try/catch: a persistence throwing synchronously would otherwise
escape as an uncaught exception and kill the
broker on connect.

## Cross-repo

The companion `aedes-persistence` commit is ready but **not yet pushed**
— that repo has no private advisory fork
to stage it in, and pushing it publicly would disclose this advisory
before there's a release. It adds
`cleanIncoming` across the async/callback/promisified layers,
`abstract.js` conformance tests, types and README,
and needs a **major (11.0.0)**: `abstract.js` tests the method
unconditionally, so every downstream goes red on a
devDep bump. Downstream checklist (mongodb, redis, level, nedb, sqlite)
is drafted.

One thing found there is worth calling out because it would have broken
production: `CallBackPersistence` always
defined `cleanIncoming`, so aedes's feature detection passed on the
wrapper and the bare delegation threw
**synchronously** on the first clean CONNECT. mongodb, redis and level
all wrap their own async persistence in
that exact class, so every one of those brokers would have crashed on
connect. Fixed at the source — the wrapper
no longer advertises a capability the wrapped implementation lacks.

## Tests

- `do not dedup a reused QoS 2 messageId after clean reconnect` — the
advisory scenario end-to-end. Fails without
the fix as a bounded ~2s assertion (`subscriber must receive the
republished message`), not a 180s hang.
- `dedup a reused QoS 2 messageId after non-clean reconnect` —
[MQTT-4.3.3-2] regression guard. Commented to say
it cannot exercise the fix, since the two paths are mutually exclusive
by construction.
- `clean session discards its QoS 2 dedup store on disconnect`
- `clean-session connect survives a persistence without cleanIncoming` —
covers the feature-detect false branch.

Full suite **319 pass / 0 fail**, lint and tsd clean.

`multiple publish and store one` now reads the stored packet *before*
`close()` instead of after. Its assertion is
about dedup storing exactly one packet; reading it post-close only
worked because the store used to outlive the
clean session, which is the bug being fixed.

## Known limitation

A `clean:false` client that publishes QoS 2 without PUBREL and never
returns still keeps its entry — aedes has no
session expiry. Pre-existing, out of scope here, worth its own issue.

fix: bound the inbound QoS 2 receive window (GHSA-5jvp-3p2v-5qgf) (#1154)

Fixes GHSA-5jvp-3p2v-5qgf. Reported by Team Atlanta.

Builds on the GHSA-p8r9 fix, already on `main` as c7acaa1 — the
dependency is real, not packaging: see
"Why it needs p8r9". Also needs `aedes-persistence` 11.0.0.

## The bug

Inbound QoS 2 packet bodies were retained in the per-client incoming
persistence map with no bound on how many
a single connection could accumulate — `queueLimit` only guards the
pre-CONNACK parser queue. Unbounded
attacker-controlled retention, so memory growth until the broker
degrades.

Trigger and full analysis are in the advisory; they stay there until it
publishes.

## Two things the first attempt got wrong

The original fix used a per-client integer counter, checked before
`await incomingStorePacket` and incremented
after. Deep review found it **did not work**, and I reproduced both
failures:

**1. The cap was bypassable by the exact flood it targets.** `enqueue`
in `lib/client.js` dispatches every packet
of a socket read chunk concurrently, so a whole chunk passed the check
before any increment landed — the cap was
bypassable by the exact flood it targets, with no `clientError` raised.

**2. It broke legitimate clients.** Two concurrent PUBLISHes with the
same messageId — an ordinary QoS 2 DUP
retransmission — both missed the store, both stored, both incremented;
the single PUBREL decremented once. The
counter drifted upward until a well-behaved retransmitting client sat at
the cap and got dropped. An availability
regression *caused by* the fix.

## The fix

The slot is reserved **synchronously**, before the store, and keyed by
**messageId**. One change closes both:
reserving at the check beats the concurrent chunk, and keying by
messageId means a DUP re-reserves its own slot
instead of consuming a second one.

On this branch the same regression test reports `maxInflightInbound
exceeded` and the cap holds.

Also fixed:

- **`pubrel` releases the slot only when `incomingDelPacket` actually
resolves.** Freeing it after a failed delete
would let the store grow past the cap. The rejection is now handled
rather than riding out of `.finally()`
  uncaught, where a duplicate PUBREL losing the race killed the process.
- **`maxInflightInbound` is clamped.** `-1`, `NaN`, `1.5` or a
non-numeric config previously took the `limit > 0`
false branch and silently disabled the security control. They now fall
back to the default; only an explicit `0`
  opts out.
- **The error names the option and the limit**, matching `queueLimit`'s
`Client queue limit reached` convention,
instead of borrowing MQTT 5 "Receive Maximum" vocabulary for a v3-only
feature.

## Why it needs p8r9

The counter is per-connection; the store it bounds is per-clientId.
Without p8r9 nothing ever cleared the incoming
store, so a client could reconnect into a fresh budget while its
previous packets were still retained — 655
reconnects still reaches the 65535 ceiling. p8r9 discards a clean
session's store when the connection ends, which
gives the reservation and the data it represents the same lifetime. On
its own this PR bounds a connection, not a
session.

## Default is 1000, not 100

MQTT 3.1.1 has no Receive Maximum to advertise the window, so a
pipelining publisher cannot know to throttle.
Benchmarked: 100 is inside the range mqtt.js reaches on a burst (60
publishes/chunk × 3 chunks was dropped), which
would have disconnected legitimate publishers on a patch release. 1000
still bounds the map far below the 16-bit
messageId ceiling. `0` restores pre-fix behaviour and is documented as
doing exactly that.

## Known limitation, documented

This caps **packets, not bytes**. aedes sets no maximum packet size and
mqtt-packet permits a 256 MB remaining
length, so the byte bound is `maxInflightInbound × max frame size`. A
byte budget or a frame limit is a separate
change; `docs/Aedes.md` says so rather than implying a memory bound the
code doesn't deliver.

Separately: growth across *distinct* client ids is a different axis that
no per-client cap closes. Worth its own
advisory.

## Tests

Seven cases in `test/qos2.js`, written against what the review actually
found rather than the happy path:

- the cap holds against a 40-packet pipelined flood in one chunk (the
bypass)
- a DUP retransmission does not consume a second slot (the availability
regression)
- completing PUBREL frees the slot — a well-behaved client is never
throttled
- a duplicate PUBREL does not crash and does not free a slot twice
- `maxInflightInbound: 0` disables the cap
- a bad `maxInflightInbound` falls back to the default instead of
disabling the cap
- the original boundary case

Full suite **327 pass / 0 fail**, lint and tsd clean.
